keyVerseText: For the Son of man shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works.
rootMeaning: The word ἕκαστος (hékastos) appears to be a superlative form derived from ἕκας (hékas), meaning 'afar.' This etymology suggests an original sense of individual distinctness or separation from the whole, emphasizing each one taken apart rather than collectively. This nuance enriches the common English glosses such as 'each' or 'every' by highlighting the particularity and singularity of the individual within a group, not just the idea of totality or all-encompassing inclusion.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, ἕκαστος occurs 83 times and is consistently translated with terms emphasizing individuality within a whole, such as 'every man' (24 times), 'every one' (14 times), and 'every' (12 times). This consistent usage reveals its function as a precise adjective that singles out each member of a group for individual consideration, whether in blessing, judgment, or responsibility. The translations reflect its role in distinguishing personal accountability and personal relation rather than collective anonymity.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, ἕκαστος underscores the biblical principle that God relates to and judges individuals personally and distinctly. It affirms that each person stands accountable before God, not as an indistinct part of a crowd but as a unique moral agent. This word reinforces the scriptural teaching that salvation, judgment, and reward are matters of personal faith and works, highlighting the seriousness of individual response to God’s revelation in Christ. It also comforts believers with the assurance that God knows and values each one personally, emphasizing the intimate nature of His sovereign care.
keyVerseReflection: Matthew 16:27 states, 'For the Son of man shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works.' Here, ἕκαστος emphasizes that the coming judgment will be comprehensive yet individually applied. Each person will receive a reward that corresponds specifically to their deeds. This word deepens the verse by affirming that no one is overlooked or generalized but each one will be personally accounted for by Christ, reflecting divine justice and personal responsibility.
